Mobility Lens
Explore six ways mobile applications differ from other applications and consider their design implications.
Input and interaction
Mobile users interact through touch, gestures, voice, and small on-screen controls
Use large touch targets, simple navigation, clear feedback, and generally, stay away from precise inputs.
Screen size, orientation, and density
Mobile devices come in varying different sizes of screen sizes, pixel density and portrait dimensions.
Create responsive layouts that can adapt to varying sizes and keeps everything readable and usable.
Lifecycle and resource constraints
Mobile apps have limited battery, memory and processing power. They can also be paused stopped and rebooted at any time.
Make sure to preserve important states, avoid unnecessary imports and background work.
Context awareness
A mobile device can detect information such as location, movement, time, connectivity, and nearby devices.
Only use this information when absolutely necessary, and ask for permission first.
Usage patterns
Mobile apps are often used in short interupted spurts, accompanied by different environments.
Make common tasks quick, save progress automatically and often, and allow users to resume where they stopped.
Security and privacy expectations
Mobile devices store personal information and may be lost, shared, or potentially through insecure networks.
Collect only necessary data, protect information, and explain permission requests.
